signals.title: AUD/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry Disconnect
signals.text: The G10 scorecard flags JPY as the weekly leader up +1.036% across 7 pairs, while AUD lags at −1.044% across 4 pairs, generating an extreme 2.081% bilateral spread. AUD/JPY trades at 106.995, sliding as broad risk-off sentiment takes hold with VIX surging 11.13% to 25.5 (elevated volatility). This JPY outperformance runs directly against carry fundamentals, where RBA at 4.85% vs BoJ at 1.25% maintains a 360bp carry advantage in favor of AUD (AONIA vs TONA provides +362bp). Australian Q3 wage price index rose 1.1% q/q against 0.8% expected, keeping RBA tightening pressure intact, yet equity weakness and safe-haven flows dominate the cross. Trade bias: Bearish AUD/JPY while broader equity risk-off persists. Catalyst: Australia Employment Change on 19 Nov (forecast 19.0k). Risk: Equity rebound and VIX dropping below 20 spark carry-driven short-covering toward 108.50.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Skew + Vol Premium
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 159.21, holding above its SMA20 (158.33), SMA50 (157.63), and SMA200 (158.76) cluster. The 160.00 threshold remains the focal watch level where verbal and physical intervention risks historically escalate. Saxo 1M 25d risk reversals print at −1.71, marking an extreme put skew that signals aggressive institutional hedging against USD/JPY downside. At the same time, USD/JPY 1M ATM implied volatility sits at 7.1% against 30-day realized volatility of 5.3%, driving a positive vol risk premium of 1.7 points. CFTC positioning shows Leveraged Funds net short JPY −23,913 contracts at the 90th percentile of its 52-week range, leaving the carry trade vulnerable if spot fails at resistance. Trade bias: Neutral/bearish USD/JPY on structural intervention ceiling. Catalyst: Japan Core CPI release on 20 Nov (forecast 2.1%). Risk: Clean daily breakout above 160.00 without official intervention triggers short-covering toward 162.00.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Crowded Spec Shorts + Technical Downtrend
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.0978, testing recent lows and sitting entirely below its falling SMA20 (1.1152), SMA50 (1.1272), and SMA200 (1.1518) in an established downtrend. CFTC Leveraged Funds hold net short EUR positions of −98,604 contracts, positioning at the 6th percentile (z = −1.58) of the 52-week distribution to reflect crowded institutional bearishness. The rate differential firmly supports the greenback, with Fed at 4.00% vs ECB at 2.65% delivering a 135bp carry advantage to USD, while US 5Y yields rose +39bp over 5 sessions led by real yields (+35bp, FRED as of 13 Nov). However, retail traders stand 85% long on Retail sentiment data, diverging sharply from the institutional short positioning and increasing liquidity trap risks near the 1.0950 base. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD in line with structural trend and carry deficit. Catalyst: Euro Area CPI YoY release at 10:00 UTC (forecast 3.2%). Risk: Upside surprise in Euro Area core inflation triggers a short squeeze through SMA20 at 1.1152.

signals.title: GBP/USD — CPI Headline Softening + Resistance
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3176, remaining pinned below its SMA20 (1.3346), SMA50 (1.3327), and SMA200 (1.3408) moving average cluster. UK headline CPI for October printed at 3.6% y/y against a 3.7% consensus, prompting UK interest rate futures to lower the probability of a December BoE rate hike from 90% down to 80%. This slight easing in terminal rate expectations trims sterling's yield support despite BoE policy rate at 4.00% matching the Fed's 4.00% (neutral 0bp spread, while SONIA vs SOFR holds a narrow −5bp GBP carry advantage). Leveraged Funds maintain an extended net long GBP position of +35,586 contracts (69.0% long, pctl 71), leaving the currency exposed to long unwinds as inflation pressure marginally decelerates. Trade bias: Bearish GBP/USD testing intraday supports. Catalyst: UK Retail Sales release on 20 Nov (forecast 0.0% m/m). Risk: Hawkish BoE commentary re-accelerating hike pricing back toward 90% and lifting spot over 1.3250.
